subject: Re: Plan rebalancing — seat-to-throughput swap + addon parity check
messages:
From: Priya Shah <pshah@novamed.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@novamed.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Plan recomposition question for upcoming renewal

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the renewal schedule yesterday. We ran the usage numbers with finance and product and want to explore swapping some of our seat-heavy license into throughput credits. The goals: reduce per-seat cost, preserve access to the feature set (especially model variants + private deployment routing), and keep a small cushion of burst seats for synchronous spikes.

Two specific asks:
- Can you map which features are tied to seat entitlement vs capacity? We need addon parity if we move seats into throughput.
- What's the discount ladder if we convert 200 seats into a 24-month reserved throughput commitment? Any stepped credits for year 1 vs year 2?

We have a tentative renewal on July 15, so ideally we get a concrete option and paperwork by Monday. Attaching our current utilization snapshot for reference.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Director of Platform Engineering
Novamed

Attachment: novamed-current-usage-20270624.csv (referenced)
From: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@novamed.com>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@novamed.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Plan recomposition question for upcoming renewal

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear asks. I sketched two pragmatic options and attached a line-item workbook + a short proposal PDF for legal/finance. TL;DR: we can convert 200 seats into a 24-month Reserved Throughput bucket with an equivalent consumption floor; you keep feature parity for: private deployment routing, model-variant access, and KV cache persistence. Addon parity (observability retention & canary rollouts) requires a small add-on fee when moving below the 300-seat threshold — I call that out in the workbook.

Options summary (high level):
1) Seat-conversion (Hybrid): Convert 150 seats now + 50 burst seats retained. You get a 12% effective discount year 1, then 8% year 2 if you commit to 24 months.
2) Throughput-first (Throughput Reserved): Convert full 200 seats into Reserved Throughput + 25 burst seats as a separate addon. You get a 16% discount year 1 and 12% year 2, with an SLA uplift available for Dedicated routing (we note pricing for SLA in the proposal).

Next steps I propose:
- Kimberly will review the discount ladder and confirm margins we can hold.
- I’ll send an updated workbook with explicit per-addon equivalency rows (so your procurement can reconcile).
- If acceptable, I’ll drop a DocuSign for the 24-month amendment and get the legal redline window started.

Doc links: HubSpot record (HS-12345) and the proposal are attached.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0191

Attachments: novamed-proposal-20270625.pdf, pricing-breakdown-novamed-20270625.xlsx
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@novamed.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Plan recomposition question for upcoming renewal

Jordan / Ben — quick internal note before we finalize: the 16% / 12% ladder in option 2 is aggressive; finance asks we hold a minimum net margin of 22% across the commitment. Two small asks to preserve our floor and still be competitive:
- Convert the 16% initial discount to 14% and extend the higher-tier SLA as a billable addon (so we don’t erode margin with SLA uplift baked in).
- Include an annual usage true-up clause (quarterly cadence) to protect against sustained over-consumption that would otherwise require additional capacity.

If Priya is okay with those tweaks I think we can sign the amendment the same day. Jordan — please patch the workbook and resend the PDF with those line items called out.

—Kimberly
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Shah <pshah@novamed.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@novamed.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Plan recomposition question for upcoming renewal

Jordan — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clarity. We reviewed the two options internally with finance. We prefer the Throughput-first option (Option 2) but need the SLA for Dedicated routing — guaranteed p99 latency target — to be part of the amendment. We understand Kimberly’s margin ask; our procurement is willing to absorb an SLA addon fee if necessary, provided the overall delta vs seat pricing stays within 9% of current ARR.

Can you:
1) Update the workbook with Kimberly’s suggested ladder tweak (14%/12%), list the SLA addon fee as a separate line, and add the quarterly true-up language.
2) Send an updated PDF + DocuSign link by EOD Monday.

If those are in place we’ll push for internal signoff and aim to sign before the July 15 renewal trigger.

Thanks,
Priya
Director of Platform Engineering, Novamed
